Splicing report¶

How much intronic RNA is detected during Dictyostelium discoideum development, and what can it tell us about splicing? This report compares total single-cell RNA (snapTotal-seq), poly(A) single-cell RNA (10x), and rRNA-depleted bulk RNA from AX4.

At 0 h and 16 h, intronic evidence makes up 0.59%–1.33% of assigned counts in the shared gene set. Detected introns are 1.08–1.17 times as long as expression-matched undetected introns. The intronic fraction is higher at 16 h in all three methods, and the poly(A) increase survives the technical checks in section 5. None of these measurements is a direct splicing rate.

Convention. Unless stated otherwise, comparisons that include poly(A) use five poly(A) cell subsets matched to snapTotal's exon depth (section 2), reported as the median and range across subsets. Section 8 collects the key numbers.

1. Data and counting¶

All three methods were recounted from their alignments with one set of rules, on 7,785 nuclear, intron-bearing protein-coding genes with a single annotated transcript.

Method Cells or libraries at 0 h / 16 h Time points
Total scRNA (snapTotal-seq) 149 / 164 cells after QC, two plates per time point 0, 16 h
Poly(A) scRNA (10x, AX4 atlas) 6,626 / 11,827 atlas cells, three tagged replicate series 0–20 h, every 4 h
Bulk total RNA (Rosengarten et al., GSE90829) 2 / 1 libraries 0–24 h, every 2 h

Choices that affect interpretation: counting is unstranded for all methods, because snapTotal does not keep strand; reads overlapping any other annotated gene are ambiguous and excluded; and a unit showing a splice through the same intron is conflicting and excluded. The intronic fraction is I / (I + E), where I counts units with any intronic base and E counts exon-only units. It is a fraction of observed evidence, not of transcripts retaining an intron.

Counting and replicate details

Only primary, uniquely mapped alignments are counted (NH = 1, MAPQ = 255). A counting unit is one cell–gene–UMI combination in single-cell data (snapTotal: valid 5-base UMIs from read 2; poly(A): Cell Ranger CB/UB tags) or one fragment in bulk data, with both mates assessed together. Each accepted unit is counted once. Exon coverage does not cancel intronic evidence in the same unit. The retained gene models are identical in the two single-cell references; the poly(A) reference also contains the act15GFP, mCerulean and mCherry reporters.

Poly(A) tags identify replicate series within each multiplexed library; that the same tag is the same series across time rests on the experimenter's records. Replicate analyses use the published tag assignments; untagged cells stay in pooled results only. Cells are not independent biological replicates. The bulk comparison at 0 and 16 h uses the retained libraries; the full bulk time course is in section 7.

2. Intronic abundance and gene detection¶

Intronic evidence is at most 1.33% of counts in every method and is higher at 16 h in all three, yet it is spread across many genes: 40%–97% of expressed genes have at least one intronic count.

Depth matching. Poly(A) has far more cells and counts than snapTotal, and deeper data detect more introns. Five random orders of poly(A) cells are therefore drawn at each time point, each stopping at snapTotal's exon-UMI total, and all counts and matching are recomputed on each subset. This matches exon depth, not capture chemistry. Bars use all cells; open circles show the five subsets.

3. Intron length¶

Detected introns are consistently longer than expression-matched controls, but only modestly: 1.08–1.17× in every method and hour.

Are introns with detectable unspliced evidence longer than expression-matched introns without it? Because a longer intron is also a bigger target for stray reads, an intron counts as detected only from reads crossing an annotated exon–intron boundary with 10 bases on each side (the anchors). Each detected intron (case, ≥2 supporting units, in ≥2 cells for single-cell data) is paired with an intron with no intronic reads (control) from a gene of similar expression. The paired ratio is 2^median log2(case length / control length), so 1.10 means about 10% longer.

Matching details

Boundary support requires one uninterrupted aligned block (no indels) with ≥10 exon and ≥10 intron bases. Targets need ≥20 intron bases and ≥10 bases in each adjacent exon. Introns with some evidence but too little to be cases are dropped from both groups. Parent genes need ≥20 exon counts and, for single-cell data, exon detection in ≥5 cells.

Matching uses log2(exon counts + 1) and, for single-cell data, log2(exon-detected cells + 1), caliper 0.25 on each, one control per case, without replacement; length is not used. A ratio is reported only with ≥20 pairs and absolute standardized mean difference < 0.1 on each variable. Brackets are the 2.5–97.5% range over 500 resamples of parent genes with matching repeated; they reflect gene sampling, not biological replicates.

5-bp: same comparison with 5-bp anchors. Brackets: 95% gene-resampling interval.

Control definition. Requiring controls to have no intronic reads at all can favour short controls. Relaxing it to "no boundary units with ≥5-bp anchors" (last column) lowers the ratios to 1.05–1.15 in snapTotal and bulk, all intervals above 1, and to 1.06–1.12 in poly(A).

At full poly(A) depth only 13% and 2% of poly(A) cases find a control (1,059 and 241 pairs), with ratios of 1.12 and 1.17; the 16 h value rests on few pairs.

Why boundary-only. In snapTotal, counting only reads fully inside introns gave length ratios of 1.89 (0 h) and 2.35 (16 h); adding boundary reads gave 1.25 and 1.18; the boundary-only analysis above gives 1.14 and 1.08. A read can lie fully inside an intron only if the intron is longer than the read, so body reads preferentially find long introns. Most of the apparent twofold effect is this detection bias; a modest effect remains in all six comparisons. (The earlier pipeline also differed in other rules, so the steps are not a clean decomposition.)

4. Gene span¶

Using the same matching at gene level (cases: ≥2 intronic units of any kind, including reads inside introns; controls: none), genes with intronic evidence are consistently shorter than matched controls in genomic span (start to end, including introns). A ratio of 0.80 means 20% shorter. Intron length and gene span use different cases, so their directions need not agree.

5. Checks on the poly(A) 16 h increase¶

The full-depth poly(A) intronic fraction rises from 0.67% at 0 h to 1.33% at 16 h (all cells). Checks for technical and compositional explanations:

Check Result
Cells The median per-cell fraction rises from 0.67% to 1.32%. Dropping the 5% of cells with the highest fractions at each time leaves 0.66% and 1.30%.
Tagged replicates All three tags rise, from 0.66%–0.67% to 1.33%–1.35% at snapTotal's depth.
Genes More genes contribute to the signal at 16 h. Removing the union of the top N contributors at either time (N = 10–500), the rise stays 2.3–2.8×; the median within-gene change is 1.65–1.76×.
Internal priming The priming signature is present at both times; whether it is stronger at 16 h depends on the window tested. Keeping sense intronic units only and applying the largest observed-minus-random excess as an adjustment, the fraction still goes from 0.44% to 0.85%.
Alignment False intronic calls occurred in 0.14% of simulated spliced reads without added errors and 1.7% with 1% errors (see denominator in the details). The increase persists under every stricter alignment filter, including requiring boundary-spanning reads (0.135% to 0.516%).
Reads per UMI 16 h has more reads per exon-only UMI (1.91 vs 1.64), but UMIs seen in only one read also show an increase (0.68% to 1.38%).

The increase persists under every check. Antisense evidence and unannotated transcripts could still contribute; adjusted values here are sensitivity checks, and sections 2 and 8 keep the original counts.

Detailed checks: cells, genes, priming, alignment and read coverage

Cells. The whole 16 h poly(A) distribution shifts towards higher intronic fractions; the increase is not confined to a few extreme cells. The median per-cell fraction rises from 0.67% to 1.32%, and removing the 5% of cells with the highest fractions leaves 0.66% and 1.30%. Per-cell fraction is only weakly related to exonic depth (Spearman ρ = -0.25 at 0 h, 0.06 at 16 h).

Internal priming. Oligo(dT) priming inside introns would place intronic UMI ends just upstream of A-rich sequence. Sense intronic ends were compared with random positions in the same introns, for two A-richness definitions and three distances. There is a priming signature at both times, but it is not consistently stronger at 16 h: the observed-minus-random excess is 6–29 percentage points at 0 h and 6–22 at 16 h, larger at 16 h in 4 of 6 settings.

show(plots.priming(priming), 'priming')

Cumulative distance from sense intronic UMI 3′ ends (solid) and random intronic positions (dashed) to the nearest downstream A-rich window (≥9 A in 10 bp); dotted line at 200 bp.

As a deliberately conservative correction, antisense intronic units (which rise from 7% to 19%) were dropped and the largest excess was subtracted as if it were primed molecules. The fraction still rises from 0.44% to 0.85%.

Alignment. Misalignment of spliced reads into introns is rare: in reads simulated from 420 real introns, 0.14% of spliced reads were called intronic (1.7% with 1% sequencing errors), and none had 10-bp boundary support. Rebuilding the counts from progressively cleaner reads keeps the increase at every tier, and requiring 10-bp boundary support strengthens it.

6. Splicing time, intron position and RNA velocity¶

At each eligible intron (section 3 rules), a second pass counts unspliced (U) units, which cross an exon–intron boundary with 10-bp anchors, and spliced (S) units, which splice exactly across the annotated intron. U/S rises from 0 h to 16 h in all three methods, and across development in bulk: measured every 2 h, bulk U/S is lowest at 0 h (1.70%), lies between 2.6% and 4.2% from 2 to 22 h, climbing after 8 h, and is highest at 24 h (5.18%). Poly(A) U/S uses all cells, not the depth-matched subsets.

How long introns persist. At steady state, U/S ≈ intron persistence time ÷ mRNA lifetime. With a 2 h mRNA half-life, this gives about 1–9 minutes in the total-RNA methods (snapTotal at 0 and 16 h, bulk at all time points), and 0.3–43 minutes across all methods and the published 0.9–9.6 h half-life range. These numbers come from the model's assumptions (steady state, equal capture of U and S, unmeasured lifetimes); they are not a measured splicing time.

Model and counting details

Per-molecule logic: if introns last 1 minute and spliced mRNA about 100 minutes, we expect about 1 unspliced copy per 100 spliced. So persistence ≈ U/S × mean spliced-mRNA lifetime (half-life / ln 2). An unspliced molecule has two boundaries where U can be counted and a spliced one only one junction, so the range includes the result halved (factor 0.5–1). Half-lives are from Shapiro et al. 1988 (selected mRNAs in amoebae), not our cells at 0 and 16 h. Developing cells need not be at steady state, and poly(A) capture can under-sample unspliced RNA. U requires no splice skip overlapping the intron; S requires no intronic aligned bases at that intron; conflicting units are excluded intron by intron, and one unit can count at several introns. The pass reproduces the section 2 counts exactly at 0 h and 16 h. Counts are pooled across cells.

Intron position. In genes with ≥3 eligible introns, comparing U/S between introns (length-adjusted odds ratio; below 1 means lower U/S at the later intron):

  • second vs first: 0.85–1.00, no consistent difference (only the bulk 16 h interval excludes 1);
  • last vs second: 0.66–0.81 in snapTotal and bulk, and 0.44–0.59 in poly(A).

Terminal introns have lower U/S. This does not identify the mechanism (splicing, 3′-end processing or detection).

Intron-position method

Each compared intron needs ≥20 U + S units. Differences in log((U + 0.5)/(S + 0.5)) are regressed on log2 length ratios; the exponentiated intercept is the reported ratio. Each gene contributes one intron pair per contrast; intervals are 2.5–97.5% over 1,000 resamples of genes (shown in the figure). First, second and last refer to eligible introns after filtering.

RNA velocity. Do velocity transitions (scVelo, stochastic model; exon-only units as spliced, intronic units as unspliced) point towards later-collected cells? Across 4–16 h, 36.4% of cells point later, against 31.6%–34.7% when unspliced counts are shuffled within each tagged replicate (central 95% of 100 shuffles; one-sided p = 0.010). 56.2% of these cells show no direction. Velocity therefore carries only a small amount of developmental information in these data.

Velocity details

666 atlas cells per tag at each of six time points (11,988 cells; smallest group 1,135); 475 velocity genes. A cell's collection-hour shift is the transition-weighted mean difference between its collection time and that of its predicted next states; mean shift +0.04 h against -0.10 to -0.06 h in shuffles. The 0 h and 20 h endpoints are excluded because they can only point one way. The per-tag rows come from one joint fit, not three independent models.

Tagged replicate Cells pointing later (4–16 h) Within-replicate null, central 95% Mean hour shift
act15GFP 39.3% 34.0%–37.6% -0.02 h
mCerulean 36.0% 30.5%–33.8% +0.08 h
mCherry 33.9% 30.3%–33.4% +0.07 h

All three tags exceed their shuffled range; act15GFP nevertheless has a negative mean shift.

7. Developmental time courses¶

Both series are counted with the section 1 rules at every time point: poly(A) every 4 h, subsampled to one fixed exon depth (snapTotal's 16 h total), and bulk every 2 h from all 23 libraries.

Intronic fraction rises through development in poly(A), less clearly in bulk. Poly(A) goes from 0.66% at 0 h to about 1.0% at 8–12 h, peaks at 1.34% at 16 h and is 1.15% at 20 h. Bulk is lowest at 0 h (0.75%), between 0.80% and 0.99% from 2 to 22 h without a steady trend, and highest at 24 h (1.16%).

Detected introns are modestly longer than controls at every time point: 1.08–1.11× in poly(A) from 4 h onwards (1.22× at 0 h) and 1.11–1.17× in bulk, with no developmental trend.

Genes with intronic evidence are shorter than matched controls at every time point, the opposite of what persistence in long genes would predict: 0.80–0.86× in poly(A) and 0.69–0.86× in bulk. In both series the ratio is highest at 0 h (0.86 and 0.86) and lower later in development.
